tool_input.command: for f in lang/en/nav.json lang/ja/nav.json; do bun -e "const f='$f';const j=await Bun.file(f).json();j.locale_en='English';j.locale_ja='日本語';await Bun.write(f, JSON.stringify(j,null,2)+'\n')"; done; cat lang/ja/nav.json; bun run codegen 2>&1 | tail -15
tool_input.description: Add language names and run codegen

result:
The site now supports English and Japanese, with a language switcher in the header on every page. `bun run typecheck` passes, `bun test` passes (8 tests, including 6 new ones for the language behaviour), and the project's catalog check (`guren check --i18n`) reports both catalogs complete with the same 29 keys. I didn't boot the app or try the switcher in a browser.

- **Remembering the choice:** `POST /locale` takes `{ locale }` (`en` or `ja`) from guests and signed-in users. It saves the choice in a `locale` cookie for one year. The framework already checks that cookie before the browser's `Accept-Language`, so a reader's pick beats the browser, and a Japanese browser gets Japanese on a first visit.
- **Invalid values:** any other value, or a missing field, fails the same way an invalid post title does, and no cookie is set.
- **Redirect back:** after a pick it returns to the page in `Referer`, or `/` when there is none. One addition you didn't ask for: it only follows a `Referer` on this site, and otherwise goes to `/`, so the switcher can't be used to send readers to another site.
- **Switcher:** it's a dropdown after the other header links and shows the current language.
- **Text:** the header links and the posts list, post page and new/edit forms now read all their labels from the catalogs. No page spells out 「記事」 itself.

**Files:**
- `lang/en/nav.json`, `posts.json`, `auth.json` are new, with Japanese twins under `lang/ja/` plus `lang/ja/messages.json`, a Japanese translation of the existing welcome message. They hold the nine required keys plus extras the pages need (form labels, search messages, the switcher's language names).
- `app/Http/Validators/LocaleValidator.ts` defines the two supported languages; `app/Http/Controllers/LocaleController.ts` handles the pick.
- `routes/web.ts` adds `POST /locale` (named `locale.update`) outside the sign-in-only group, and `src/app.ts` now lists both languages.
- `resources/js/components/Layout.tsx` has the translated header (with a new Home link) and the switcher. `resources/js/pages/posts/{Index,Show,New,Edit}.tsx` read their text from the catalogs.
- The `.guren/*.gen.ts` files were regenerated with `bun run codegen`.
- `tests/LocaleController.test.ts` covers the defaults, browser detection, a pick beating the browser, the redirects and cookie, and rejected values.
